source_text: How about running the machine in the "forward direction" until it works rather than trying to reset it time and time again and failing each time?  I don't actually know how the latter is even possible, but it seems prevalent.

fragments.text: How about running the machine in the "forward direction" until it works rather than trying to reset it time and time again and failing each time?
I don't actually know how the latter is even possible, but it seems prevalent.

reply_text:
Yes, and I've written that into the candidate as the way the machine is to be run (commit `f94403d3d`).

**How the resetting happened.** Every click began a new run from nothing: a new opportunity id, the readiness checks, selection from scratch. What the previous run had reached was never the starting state of the next one. Click 15 published four interpretations and then failed at the re-decision; click 16 started over. Click 19 chose a target, dispatched an author and got a refusal; click 20 started over and walked into the same refusal. So each failure threw away the run, and the next click had to get past every earlier step again before it could reach the step that had failed. I treated that as the normal way of working; nothing forced it.

**What forward means, as I've written it.** There is one continuing run with a durable state: the field, the chosen task, the phase reached, and the results so far. Each invocation advances that state by one step. A failure leaves the state at the failed step. The failure is handled as an incident, and then the same run continues from that step. Nothing already achieved is redone.

This also lines the three pieces up. The Lean model is a state and a step function, the verification applies the step repeatedly to one persisted state, and the running machine does the same. Before, the model would have described one thing and the clicks another.

**What it needs.** Two things: the run state saved at each phase boundary, and an entry point that continues from a saved state. A quick search of the runner found checkpoint evidence being written and no resume entry point. That's a search, not a read, so I've asked codex-6 to confirm it against the code.

**Where forward would start.** The last run's state is real: M-descriptive-essay-of-the-stack was chosen, an author was dispatched, and the author refused because invariants I1–I6 are unaudited. Going forward from there, the refusal is recorded against that attempt, and the next step is either to hand an agent the missing audit or to choose the next task.

codex-6's queued job (`invoke-1790752734211-28811-86ecfc6d`, `park-8606bd06…`) re-reads the file when it starts, so their yes or no will cover this too.
